A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 32-page versions of the same AIGB-Pearl paper. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–I without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v4 reports original simulated bidding experiments, Taobao A/B tests, evaluator experiments and supplementary analyses, including Tables 1–5 and 8–13.

after.justification: v5 reports the retained original simulation and Taobao A/B results, including the TargetROAS experiment in Table 8, alongside evaluator results and revised training-stability curves.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix E retain the same evaluator, KL-Lipschitz-constrained planner, synchronous coupling, LLM embeddings and training losses. The first-price adaptation in Appendix G already appears in v4.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same simulated and Taobao bidding tasks, unseen advertisers, TargetROAS, multiple-policy offline data and first-price auctions. The revised training diagnostics introduce no different dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmarks, including USCB, BCQ, CQL, IQL, MORL, MOPO, DT and DiffBid. Appendix F.5 retains the comparator labeled 'Offline RL with Bootstrapping'.

E3.justification: Appendix F.5 drops online-rate and bad-case-rate metrics. It labels the former cumulative-reward plot 'scores' without clarifying whether the measured quantity changed; cost rate becomes cost ratio with the same cost/budget definition. Other stated evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The training-stability analysis loses the online-rate and bad-case-rate diagnostics, reducing evidence about early budget exhaustion and pathological trajectories. The constraint ablations, evaluator analyses, distribution-robustness experiment and hyperparameter study are retained.

E5.justification: v5 Figures 10–11 add mean curves and shaded bands labeled 'Mean ± Std' to the individual seed traces. Both versions specify ten seeds; no increase in runs is stated. Existing cross-validation uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 10 and the cost/budget plot, matched from v4 Figure 13 to v5 Figure 11, display different seed trajectories. Online-rate and bad-case-rate result series are removed. The broad stability ranking and all numerical table entries remain unchanged; the PDFs do not explain whether the replacement curves reflect reruns or different processing.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Theorems 1–3, proofs in Appendix C and performance-range derivation in Appendix D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about evaluator-guided bidding, constrained exploration, synchronous coupling and superior performance. The claim of greater training stability is also retained.

C2.justification: Appendix F.5 retains the interpretation that AIGB-Pearl learns more smoothly and consistently than bootstrapped offline RL. Explanations of constraint benefits, evaluator accuracy, distribution robustness and applicability to first-price and online settings are unchanged.

D1.justification: The algorithm and evaluator implementation details, hardware specifications, experimental settings in Tables 6–7 and hyperparameter information in Appendix F.8 are retained. No new procedural explanation accompanies the replacement learning curves.

R1.justification: The references and related-work discussion in Appendix A are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to offline RL and generative auto-bidding methods.

P1.justification: Appendix F.5 has a shortened metric list and updated terminology and figure references. Section 2.1 changes 'a priori' to 'a prior'. The section order and almost all other prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Appendix F.5's four figures become two: Figure 10 is redrawn, v4 Figure 13 becomes the redrawn Figure 11, and v4 Figures 11–12 are removed. Axes, legends, styling and uncertainty shading change, while several appendix tables and sections shift position.

improvement.justification: The added mean and standard-deviation summaries improve uncertainty presentation. However, removing online-rate and bad-case-rate results loses distinct evidence about budget exhaustion and pathological trajectories, while the replacement 'score' curves are not clearly related to the former cumulative rewards. This modestly weakens the clarity and breadth of support for the retained stability and safety claims. The central method, theory and benchmark results remain intact.
